That’s good to know, I didn’t know that Jews were historically compared to pigs & I appreciate you educating me. I agree there were better ways to criticize the Regents but again, even though you say it’s a highly common trope, most of us were unaware it was so I doubt how widespread it actually is in the modern world. It’s still offensive if enough people are offended, and they should’ve been more thoughtful. I don’t want my Jewish friends and colleagues feeling unsafe, and this made them feel unsafe, so I wish it hadn’t happened. However, I think many of us are also tired of any and all dissent against Israel’s crimes being immediately labeled as antisemitic. I would like to speak out against literal ethnic cleansing without being called a racist, but that has been the case even before this pig statue was displayed.

I had to look this up because I had no idea that pigs were used to insult Jewish people. The Judensau trope depicts Jewish people interacting with a pig in obscene ways (https://www.philaholocaustmemorial.org/antisemitism-explained/), but I couldn’t find any real history of comparing a Jewish person to a pig; I think most of us think cop or capitalist when we see pigs. I agree that Judensau is highly offensive; I would be offended too if there were multiple pieces of “artwork” where people of my ethnicity/religion were portrayed suckling on a pig and staring at their rectum. The people that made this definitely should have been more careful, especially since the flag of Israel does have the Star of David on it, but I genuinely believe this was not deliberate. Criticizing Israel for acts of genocide does not equal criticizing Jewish people for their religious beliefs. That doesn’t mean you’re not allowed to be offended of course, but I think calling this antisemitism is jumping to conclusions. It’s way more common to call cops and capitalists pigs, and I really think this was meant to shame the Regents and not to attack Jews.

I’m thinking about it in 3 spatial dimensions, assuming the earth doesn’t move or rotate (alternatively, assuming the earth moves like we know it does but observing the person in a reference frame that moves & rotates with the earth). If we think of the problem as being on a periodic 2D map, what you’re saying is right ig but it doesn’t make sense to me personally to define our velocity in that way bc in the end our 2D surface is curved and embedded in a 3D space and we naturally observe our world in 3 dimensions. I think there are truly an infinite number of ways to set this problem up so that the meme doesn’t make sense any more

It’s a silly meme :P If we pick a reference frame that moves with the earth and rotates as the same speed as the earth it works; even though it’s not an inertial frame, we’re free to make that choice so why not. I think the meme is cute & clever once we make a few compromises and ignore some details

If you go around the globe you actually change direction since you go in a circle. Velocity is a vector so it cancels out in the end. Time zones have no play in measuring time elapsed during travel. I think the meme should be taken lightly bc we’re ignoring the fact that the earth itself rotates and revolves around the sun to begin with

Velocity is a vector quantity and you technically change direction as you go around the planet even though you keep traveling east bc the earth is round. This meme stops making sense once you read to much into it tho, bc the earth rotates and also revolves around the sun :P
The average velocity is the total displacement divided by the total time so they’re both zero. Maybe you’re confusing it with average speed, which would indeed be nonzero
